card.summary: The HALT Fentanyl Act permanently places fentanyl-related substances as a class into schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act, subjecting them to the same quantity thresholds and criminal penalties as fentanyl analogues. It also creates a new alternative registration process for certain schedule I research and adjusts various research requirements under the Controlled Substances Act.

summary: The HALT Fentanyl Act permanently places fentanyl-related substances as a class into schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act, subjecting them to the same regulatory controls and criminal penalties as fentanyl analogues. It also creates alternative and expedited registration processes for certain schedule I research involving these substances, modifies research site and personnel requirements, and outlines rules for manufacturing small quantities for research purposes.

affected_groups.effect: Will face criminal penalties triggered by the same quantity thresholds as fentanyl analogues, such as a 10-year mandatory minimum prison term for offenses involving 100 grams or more.
affected_groups.group: Individuals involved in offenses related to fentanyl-related substances

affected_groups.effect: Gain access to expedited registration pathways, single registrations for related research sites within the same city or county, and exemptions from separate manufacturing registrations for small quantities used in research.
affected_groups.group: Researchers and practitioners studying schedule I controlled substances

key_provisions: Permanently places fentanyl-related substances as a class into schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act.
Applies the same quantity thresholds and criminal penalties to offenses involving fentanyl-related substances as those involving fentanyl analogues.
Establishes a new, alternative registration process for certain schedule I research tied to federal agencies or investigational new drug exemptions.
Permits a single researcher registration to cover multiple related research sites within the same city or county under certain conditions.
Allows registered researchers to perform small-scale manufacturing activities of the research substance without needing a separate manufacturing registration.
Expresses the sense of Congress agreeing with the judicial interpretation of the Controlled Substances Act in United States v. McCray.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The HALT Fentanyl Act permanently places fentanyl-related substances as a class into schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act, subjecting them to the same regulatory controls and criminal penalties as fentanyl analogues. It also creates alternative and expedited registration processes for certain schedule I research involving these substances, modifies research site and personnel requirements, and outlines rules for manufacturing small quantities for research purposes.
summary_detail.significance: This bill permanently establishes class-wide schedule I control and criminal penalties for fentanyl-related substances while altering administrative research hurdles for scientific and federal investigators.
